thread:
sam-support: Hey @maria — customer ACME reports users suddenly can't open Project Settings or Billing after SSO group consolidation. They see a 403 UI page and `permission denied` from the API. Can you eyeball?

maria: Which project + sample user? Any logs / repro steps from the console?

sam-support: Project: acme-prod. Affected user: alice@acme.com. Steps she did:
1) SSO login -> lands in console
2) Click Projects -> selects acme-prod
3) Click Settings -> UI shows 403 and yellow banner "You don't have permission to view this page"
4) API call returned: `{"code":403,"message":"permission denied"}` from /v1/projects/acme-prod/settings

okta-sync-bot: SCIM sync completed: 2026-03-10T13:12:04Z — action: merge_groups -> created consolidated group 'acme-users' (merged 3 external groups). Preserved original timestamps, new external_group_id: grp_9f3b2c.

ida: Do we have audits for rolebindings for acme-prod? Specifically any bindings referencing external group ids that might not exist after the merge?

maria: pulling rolebinding list now. Quick grep shows project-admin bindings point to external group ids: grp_a1, grp_b2, grp_c3. After merge those exact ids aren't present; only grp_9f3b2c exists. So looks like rolebindings reference old external IDs.

ben: That matches a known gap: SCIM group merge replaces/creates a new external_group_id rather than aliasing old ids. Our rolebinding lookup is keyed by external_group_id. If the merge didn't create backward aliases we lose bindings.

ops-luis: Can we repro locally? I have a repro script. Using alice's id_token and calling list-rolebindings:```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/acme-prod/rolebindings"``` Response: 200 with bindings for users + service accounts, but none for group ids. Then checking access:```curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/acme-prod/settings"``` -> 403.

maria: Temporary mitigation: I can run our internal group->role rebuild job for org acme. That will map group names to existing rolebindings where possible. Before running, can we confirm no data loss risk?

ben: Safe to run read-only mode first: POST /internal/admin/rebuild-group-bindings?dry_run=true body: `org: "acme"` — this will show proposed changes. Then run without dry_run to apply. Also add we should trigger SCIM to create group aliases for old ids if Okta supports it.

sam-support: Can you do dry_run and paste output here? Customer is blocked on billing changes.

maria: Dry run result: proposes 3 new bindings — map grp_9f3b2c -> project.admin, project.billing.viewer -> true. No deletions. Looks good.

ops-luis: Running apply now... POST /internal/admin/rebuild-group-bindings body: `org: "acme"`

okta-sync-bot: SCIM sync note: incoming merge action did not set "previous_external_ids" attribute. Consider enabling "preserveExternalIds" flag in provisioning to maintain aliases.

maria: Done — rebuild job applied. @sam-support can you ask alice to retry?

acme-alice: I just retried. Settings and Billing load fine now. I can toggle billing alerts. Thank you! :tada:

sam-support: Closing loop with customer and drafting internal postmortem. Root cause: SCIM group consolidation created a new external group id without aliasing the old ids; our rolebindings keyed to external ids didn't automatically migrate. Action items: 1) support team emailed account team, 2) engineering to add name-based fallback during binding lookup, 3) docs: recommend configuring SCIM to preserve external ids or enable aliasing.

ben: I'll follow up with a fix to make binding lookup resilient (first try external_id then fallback to group name). Also adding alert when many bindings become orphaned after a sync.

maria: Thanks everyone. I'll mark this resolved on the support ticket and add the dry_run output to the ticket.

sam-support: Nice quick turnaround. Filing a short incident note and tagging eng infra. :thumbsup:
